summary: The XRD analysis in this paper demonstrates a systematic shift in diffraction peak positions from FAPbBr3 to CsPbBr3 as the Cs/FA molar ratio (X) increases in core/shell perovskite nanocrystals. This indicates successful formation of FAPbBr3/CsPbBr3 core/shell structures with tunable composition and lattice parameters.

key_findings.finding: XRD peaks for FAPbBr3/CsPbBr3 core/shell nanocrystals systematically shift to higher 2θ values as the Cs/FA molar ratio (X) increases, with peak positions moving from those characteristic of FAPbBr3 toward those of CsPbBr3.
All samples, including pure FAPbBr3, pure CsPbBr3, and intermediate core/shell compositions, exhibit broad XRD peaks, indicating nanocrystalline character across the series.
No additional phases or impurity peaks are reported in the XRD patterns for any composition, suggesting phase purity is maintained throughout the core/shell series.

scientific_interpretation: The observed continuous shift in XRD peak positions with increasing Cs content (X) in the FAPbBr3/CsPbBr3 core/shell nanocrystals suggests successful epitaxial overgrowth of the CsPbBr3 shell on the FAPbBr3 core, resulting in a gradual lattice contraction. The absence of new peaks or phase separation implies that the core/shell interface is coherent and that the system remains single-phase at the nanoscale, at least within the detection limits of XRD. The broadness of the peaks across all samples is consistent with the nanocrystalline size regime and supports the conclusion that the structural integrity of the perovskite lattice is preserved during shell growth.
limitations: Only one figure (fig_2) contains XRD data, limiting the ability to cross-validate findings with other structural characterization techniques within the XRD domain.
No quantitative analysis of phase fractions, crystallite size, or lattice parameters is provided in the XRD data.
The absence of reported impurity or secondary phases is based on the lack of additional peaks, but minor phases below the detection limit of XRD cannot be ruled out.
Peak broadening is attributed to nanocrystallinity, but no Scherrer analysis or explicit size estimation from XRD is presented.
